0.0.n: Names the season that arrives in 春になる.

0.1.n: Marks the resulting state with なる; literally, the season becomes spring.

0.2.n: Plain form of なる, meaning become; 春になる describes the arrival of spring.

0.3.n: After a plain-form verb, と introduces a predictable result or regular occurrence.

0.5.n: Used with の before 人 to describe a large number of people.

0.6.n: Links 多く to 人, forming the expression for many people.

0.7.n: Japanese nouns usually do not change form for plural meanings.

0.8.n: Marks 多くの人 as the people doing the action.

0.9.n: 桜 can name cherry trees or their blossoms; the blossoms are the attraction here.

0.10.n: Marks 桜 as what people go to see.

0.11.n: The stem of 見る, made by dropping る, connects to に行きます to express a purpose.

0.12.n: Marks the purpose of going: seeing the blossoms.

0.13.n: Polite form of 行く; here it describes a customary activity, not an action happening right now.

1.0.n: Names one of the places where the blossoms bloom.

1.1.n: Lists examples rather than giving a complete list.

1.2.n: With の近く, this identifies what the nearby location is close to.

1.3.n: Links 川 to 近く; 川の近く means near rivers.

1.4.n: A location noun here, used with 川の to describe the area near rivers.

1.5.n: Marks the places where the blossoms appear.

1.6.n: Added after に to make the locations the topic of the sentence.

1.8.n: 色 means color; ピンク色 names the color of the blossoms.

1.9.n: Connects the color noun ピンク色 to 花 so it describes the blossoms.

1.10.n: Refers to the cherry flowers mentioned in the previous sentence.

1.12.n: Combines with に to describe how the blossoms bloom, giving the scene a peaceful feeling.

1.13.n: Turns 静か into a description of how the action happens.

1.14.n: Polite form of 咲く, a verb used for flowers opening.

2.0.n: 々 repeats the preceding character; 人々 explicitly refers to multiple people.

2.1.n: Marks 人々 as the topic: the sentence describes what people do.

2.2.n: A borrowed word for sheets; here it refers to ground coverings people sit on.

2.3.n: Marks シート as what people spread out.

2.4.n: て-form of 広げる, linking spreading the mats to the activity that follows.

2.6.n: Describes an unhurried pace, rather than specifically an absence of sound.

2.7.n: Optionally follows ゆっくり when it describes how an action is done.

2.8.n: Refers to the blossoms people enjoy viewing during their outing.

2.9.n: Marks 桜 as what people look at.

2.10.n: The stem of 見る connects to ながら to describe an action happening alongside another.

2.11.n: Attaches to a verb stem to show the same people doing two activities at once.

2.12.n: Pairs with 過ごす to describe how people spend part of their day.

2.13.n: Marks 時間 as what is spent.

2.14.n: Polite form of 過ごす; 時間を過ごす describes passing time in a particular way.

3.0.n: Points back to the blossom-viewing activity just described.

3.1.n: Marks これ as the activity being given a name.

3.3.n: Names the custom described above; 花 means flower and 見 refers to viewing.

3.5.n: Marks 花見 as the quoted name used for this activity.

3.6.n: Polite form of 言う; in AをBと言います, it gives B as the name for A.

0.lit: When it becomes spring, many people go to see cherry blossoms.
0.tip: A verb stem plus に行く means going somewhere to do that action.

1.lit: In parks and near rivers, pink-colored flowers quietly bloom.
1.tip: 静かに describes how the flowers bloom: に turns 静か into a description of the action.

2.lit: People spread out mats and leisurely spend time while viewing cherry blossoms.
2.tip: 見ながら means while viewing; ながら connects two activities performed by the same people.

3.tip: AをBと言います means to call A by the name B.
